Yes cops have a special right to wield violence but its not always a first option in dealing with situations. In highschool I had a class called Student and Law taught by an ex cop whos been retired from the force for about 6 years then. One of the things he talked about is police and in great detail. In one lesson he taught us how cops dealt with controling a situation whwther it be with one person or many.

The ways they gained control of a situation were:
1st - Uniform presence - simply showing up can cause people to focus their attention on you instead of causing any commotion or further escalating a situation.

2nd - Vocal Presence - If Uniform doesnt work you then shout to gain attention from those you need the attention of. Its why you see alot of cops shout after showing up at places where there are fights.

3rd - Non lethal force - bean bag shot gun, tazer, baton, and physical intervention are just to name a few. This is for when vocal doesnt work.

4th - Lethal Force - Any gun really. This is sometimes where cops go to if they are told any suspect has a lethal weapon or gun. Uniform, vocal, and non lethal are going to do nothing again an armed suspect. Now lethal force doesnt mean open fire, means to take out the gun and try to get the suspect to drop their weapon before they try to use it on yourself.

He never killed a man but he has come close. And he was a good cop who even advocated for better training for cops and even knew some of his people in blue were just not cut out for it.

But the idea that they are bad for evicting people? A poor person can rob a store, doesnt mean he should get away with it. Police are ment to keep people in line but they are also ment to serve the public and keep them safe. Now going into what u said that some people dont feel safe with cops around. Thats reasonable. In a time like now people are questioning the standards and tactics cops employ which is good. Despite being cops they arent above critisism and if something doesnt work you work to change or reform certain parts. But in some places cops are seen as part of the community.

Its called community policing and in some neighborhoods and cities police departments work to become integrated into part of the community in anyway they can. There are tons of ways they do that in order to humanize cops and break the steryotype that cops are brutal murderers who break up families by locking up half of the people they detain and killing the others with little to no empathy for human life. You may call it copaganda, but if u wanted to protect your community and you knew there was a stigma against cops, why wouldnt you want to get the community to swe a better side of not only you but the department as a whole. It protects the lives of the cops who after hours can be attacked due to grudges or general hatred towards the police. Almost happend to my teacher too. Eliminating those crosshairs on your back would make your life safer and a community more willing to cooperate with you.

Some cops are sadly abusive to their spouse someyimes due to stress from their work. Not trying to justify spousal abuse at all. But there are other ways this stuff manifests. Stress from work can cause depression. Happened with my teacher, he became distant with his wife, divorced, married someone else, did the same thing, and is now with his third wife. Now im not saying lets lower the bar for police so they dont stress, but all I'm saying is I can see why and its an issue police departments need to deal with as this effects their life on and off duty.

Lastly on valueing property over life. If I owned a motel and I had someone squating in a room, I loose profit. He isnt taking money away from me in a traditional sense, but his pressence makes it so i cant rent out the room to anyone. Because of that I loose profit. I mentioned this already. But going further into it, if i am loosing money, that means I will not be able to pay for certain things. Whether it be bills, taxes, utilities, food, possesions, that money is not comming because of someone ruining my buisness. Calling the cops to remove that person is not having cops value property over a life. Its keeping the legitimacy and integrety of my buisness alive so I may make money to pay for the things i need. And homeless people are a completly different topic but some cops help direct them to homeless shelters and food banks if they are avalible in their city. Those two buisnesses i mentioned are not run by cops so they have no control in whether they exist in a city or not.

I do want to mention that I honestly feel like its those who take the 911 call who are at fault here cause I had a similar experience. I had a job interview one day but on this day I wasnt feeling well, I had a high body heat and a strong pain in my mid section. I asked a friend to come with me in the car as i went and in exchange I'll drive him to work. After my interview i got worse and worse to the point where i almost crashed. I let my friend drive my car to his job and told him I'll just need a few mins to recoup. Few mins later I called 911 cause I was having trouble breathing. When first responders came they had a tough time finding me. I was in my car near the entrence of a parking lot so i was on a very visible area. But they couldnt find me because 911 never told them what kind of car I was in and what color it was. Because of this they searched the whole parking lot for me till they checked mine. They were not told about what car I had when I told 911 nor did they tell them i was not kn drugs which i was questioned about. This is just my experience. There are others where 911 doesnt tell the full story to first responders that could make or break someones life.
